requirement: In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. Raw HTML means an HTML block, an HTML comment, or an inline HTML tag including its attributes; text between inline tags is ordinary Markdown. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
rationale:
I found no gap. Every obligation maps to code reachable from the two `{impl}` items, and each has a test that runs that code and asserts the outcome.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Escaped roles stay literal and are not references.** `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_roles]` skips any `{` that `is_escaped`. It is reached from `src/terms.rs#fn[direct_references]` through `referenced_terms`.
- **Roles in inline code, fenced code and raw HTML stay literal.** `reference_roles` skips roles inside the ranges from `src/lib.rs#fn[protected_ranges]`.
  - `protected_ranges` collects pulldown-cmark ranges for `Tag::CodeBlock`, `Event::Code`, `Event::Html` (HTML blocks and comments) and `Event::InlineHtml` (inline tags, including their attributes).
  - Text between inline tags is not in any of these ranges, so it stays ordinary Markdown.
  - Outside Markdown (`markdown == false`) no ranges are protected.
- **Colon-fenced references in code or raw HTML stay literal.** The `{impl}` item `src/fenced.rs#fn[markdown_fences]` marks each line `protected` when it overlaps `protected_ranges`, then calls `find_fences`.
- **A `{req}` directive in a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role do not define a requirement.**
  - `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` ignores any opener that overlaps `code_block_ranges`.
  - It only recognizes line-start colon fences, so an inline `{req}` role is never a definition.
  - `direct_references` calls `definition_blocks` for requirements inputs, so this code is reachable from an `{impl}` item.
- **Term references in the subject text and in requirements inputs.** `direct_references` implements this. It scans bodies as Markdown through `referenced_terms`, and `reference_roles` applies the protections above.
- **Which files are Markdown.** `crate::outline::is_markdown_path` is called from `direct_references`. Other callers (`evidence.rs#fn[file_references]`, `lib.rs#fn[text_references]`) only pass the flag to `reference_roles` and `markdown_fences`, so they add no decisions of their own.

**Tests, each carrying a `{test}` reference to the subject**
- **Escaped roles, inline code and fenced code:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal]`. It also covers escaped backslashes.
- **Raw HTML:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal]` covers an HTML block, a comment, an inline tag attribute and text between tags. It also checks that non-Markdown text gets no protection.
- **Colon fences in HTML blocks, comments and tag attributes:** `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_in_raw_html_stay_literal]`.
- **Fenced `{req}` examples and legacy `{req}` roles:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal]` and `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal`. Both run `definition_blocks` through `replace_definitions`.
- **Requirement bodies:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_in_requirement_bodies_are_scanned_as_markdown]`.
- **All Markdown extensions, with plain text as a negative:** `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_markdown_extension_keeps_escaped_and_code_roles_literal]`. It also covers a colon fence nested in a code fence.
- **Evidence coverage:** `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_references_are_covered_by_evidence_inputs]`.
- **Term dependencies:** `src/terms.rs#mod[tests]/fn[term_dependencies_of_every_markdown_extension_skip_literal_roles]` and `tests/definitions.rs#fn[literal_term_roles_in_subject_and_requirements_inputs_need_no_definition]`.

I found no unspecified extra behavior in the `{impl}` code.
